name: AIRDO
description: White, with a sky-blue band and a yellow band (a thin white line between them) sweeping up from the belly under the wing's trailing edge, aft along the crown and on up the fin; the fin's leading edge and tip sky blue, the yellow running out at its trailing edge, its lower rear white, 'AIR DO' in black across it. Very large black 'AIR DO' from behind the forward door across the windows, '北海道の翼' (Wings of Hokkaido) small above it. White engines; yellow winglets with Bear Do, the airline's polar-bear mascot, on their inner faces.

logos.description: Regional Plus Wings' small mark (the holding company AIRDO shares with Solaseed Air since 2022): a gray 'RP' in a circle with a plus, 'Regional Plus' under it, just behind the cockpit windows.

titles.style: AIRDO's wordmark, very large black geometric capitals from behind the forward door across the windows (the glass through the letters), 'AIR' set a little lower than 'DO' so the line rises toward the tail on the left side (toward the nose on the right).
'Wings of Hokkaido' small in Japanese over the title's start.
The wordmark in black across the fin's middle, over the white line and the blue's edge.

notes: Measured on JA12AN (737-700, left, 2022-01-18) fitted to shapes/B737.json; the newest photos (JA11AN 2026-06-09, JA612A and JA605A 2026) show it unchanged. The blue's front edge reads x 0.566 at the belly, near upright to the window line, then curving aft to the crown at 0.645; the yellow from 0.604-0.685 at the belly to the fin's root; near the crown the edges were set from JA11AN (2026, from the ground), since JA12AN's high camera shows the crown foreshortened. On the fin the edges were read against the photo's own fin outline (the fitted outline's trailing edge was ~30 px out). Right side (JA16AN, JA612A): mirrored. Bear Do, AIRDO's own polar-bear mascot, is painted on the winglets' inner faces only (seen on the far winglet from either side); the outer faces are plain yellow, so it isn't a logo here: the schema has no place for a winglet's inner face (a mark for it, ADO/bear-do, is proposed for Skyarium). The 767s, without winglets, carry no Bear Do. Not drawn: the small figure sticker beside the forward door on JA11AN, the registration.
history: New 2026-11-22. AIRDO (Hokkaido International Airlines) flies 737-700s and 767-300ERs within Japan from Sapporo (New Chitose).
